PrivateType is a private, local push-to-talk dictation app for Windows. Hold a shortcut, speak, and release it to insert text into the field where dictation began, without cloud recognition. Nothing you say is written to disk.

## New in this release

### Second speech model: Parakeet

- Choose between two local NVIDIA models on first launch, or later in the new **Settings → Model** page: the default Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming 0.6B, or Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3.
- Parakeet detects the language itself (25 European languages) and writes the final text in one pass after you release the shortcut. The bubble shows **Transcribing…** until the text is inserted; a minute of speech takes a few seconds on the recorded test machine.
- **Show a live preview with Parakeet** (on by default) refreshes what you have said so far about once a second while you speak. It uses more CPU; turn it off in **Settings → Model**.
- Vocabulary boosting works with Nemotron only. **Fix phrases after dictation** applies to both models, and the shortcut's language still chooses which corrections apply.
- **Settings → Model** downloads the other model, switches between them, and deletes a model you no longer need. Parakeet is about 681 MiB and licensed CC-BY-4.0.

### Recent dictations

- If you switch windows before a dictation finishes, the text is no longer lost. Press **Win+Shift+V**, or choose **Recent dictations…** in the bubble menu, to see your recent dictations, newest first. Ones that could not be inserted are marked **Not inserted**.
- Press Enter or click an entry to paste it into the window you were in. If that window can't take the text, it is copied so you can paste it with Ctrl+V. **Delete** or **×** removes one entry, and **Clear all** removes everything.
- **Settings → Recent dictations** keeps them until PrivateType exits (default), for 1 hour, for 15 minutes, or not at all. They stay in memory only, at most 50, and are never written to disk or diagnostics. With **Don't keep**, Win+Shift+V goes back to Windows.
- **Show pasted dictations in Win+V clipboard history** is off by default. Cloud clipboard skips dictated text either way.

### Custom vocabulary

- Teach PrivateType the names, acronyms, and technical terms it keeps getting wrong in **Settings → Vocabulary**, also reachable from **Vocabulary…** in the bubble and tray menus.
- Phrases can apply to every language or to one language only.
- One **Strength** setting (Low, Normal, Strong) controls how hard the model leans toward your phrases. On PrivateType's tests, Normal raised correctly spelled technical terms from about 1 in 5 to about half without inserting them into unrelated sentences.
- Vocabulary stays on this computer and is only given to the local speech engine.
- **Teach from last dictation…** in the bubble menu shows your last sentence as words: click the ones it got wrong, type the correct spelling, and add as many fixes as the sentence needs before saving them together. **Open vocabulary** jumps to the language you saved to. Each fix also remembers the words it replaced.
- **Fix phrases after dictation** corrects the finished sentence before it is inserted: spoken forms such as "three D printing" or "fusion three sixty" become "3D printing" and "Fusion 360" (numbers and letters in English or Polish), and taught **Heard as → Write as** pairs are applied. Turn it off or edit the pairs in **Settings → Vocabulary**. Only your spelling is kept.
- **Packs** let you share phrase lists: import a `.privatetype-vocabulary.json` file after reviewing every phrase and choosing its language, turn packs on or off, edit them, or export your own phrases. PrivateType never downloads packs.
- Each dictation uses at most 200 phrases from your list and the switched-on packs for its language; up to 1,000 phrases can be stored.

### 32 recognition languages

- Each shortcut can now use Automatic or any of the 32 languages and regions the Nemotron model recognizes out of the box, from English (United States and United Kingdom), Spanish, French, and Portuguese in two regions each, to German, Italian, Dutch, Ukrainian, Russian, Czech, Swedish, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified), and more.
- Polish and English keep their default shortcuts. Existing shortcuts carry over unchanged.
- The app's own interface stays in English, and the recording status now reads "Listening" in every language.

### Press to start, press again to stop

- **Settings → Shortcuts → Shortcut behavior** can now be **Press to start and stop** instead of holding the shortcut. If the model is still loading, listening starts by itself when it is ready.

### Text now arrives in one step

- **Insert text by → Pasting** is the new default. The whole dictation lands at once, so pressing Enter right away can no longer send half-typed text.
- Your previous clipboard is put back afterwards, unless you copied something new in the meantime.
- Dictated text is kept out of cloud clipboard, and out of Windows clipboard history unless you opt in (see Recent dictations).
- **Typing characters** is still available for apps where Ctrl+V does not paste, such as Vim or PuTTY. It never touches the clipboard.
- Settings saved by earlier versions switch to Pasting; change it back in **Settings → Shortcuts → Insert text by** if you prefer typing.

### Updated Nemotron model file

- PrivateType now uses NVIDIA's re-converted Nemotron file (revision `ea30d66`), which recognizes speech exactly as before and includes the tokenizer that custom vocabulary needs.
- The first start of this version downloads it once more (about 708 MiB). The previous copy in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PrivateType\models` is left untouched and can be deleted after closing older versions.

### Settings

- Language names are shown in full, and the remove-shortcut button is now compact.
- Settings are stored in a new format. An older PrivateType version reading these settings would treat every shortcut as Polish; keep each version's own settings folder if you plan to switch back.

### Bubble and exit reliability

- The bubble menu now closes when you click anywhere else or press a dictation shortcut. Previously it could stay on screen because the bubble never takes focus.
- Quitting right after a dictation no longer leaves PrivateType running invisibly with its menu still on screen. Exit now waits at most a few seconds for the last dictation to finish.
- After sleep, a display change, or unlocking Windows, the bubble is brought back on screen and on top. It also returns to its saved position if it ends up outside every display.
- A drag that Windows interrupted no longer keeps the bubble stuck to the pointer.

## Also since v1.0.7

Versions 1.0.8 and 1.1.0 were prepared but never published; their improvements are included above and here.

- Microphones are remembered by their Windows device identity, so plugging in or removing another device no longer switches dictation to the wrong microphone. Full microphone names are shown in Settings, and an existing choice is carried over when its name identifies exactly one device.
- If Windows never reports that the shortcut was released, PrivateType notices the key is up and finishes the dictation instead of recording indefinitely.
- The local speech engine picks a free local port each time it starts, and the model unloads after the selected idle time even if you never dictate after starting PrivateType.
- An invalid value in the settings file resets only that setting, and PrivateType names which settings were reset. "Text not inserted" messages explain why, and the remaining Polish-only error messages are in English.
- Updated to .NET 10, the current long-term-support release.

## Download and start

1. Download `PrivateType-1.2.0-win-x64.zip` and `PrivateType-1.2.0-win-x64.zip.sha256` below.
2. Verify the SHA-256 checksum.
3. Extract the complete ZIP into a writable folder.
4. Open `PrivateType 1.2.0` and double-click `PrivateType.exe`.
5. Choose a speech model on first launch and approve its separate download if it is not already in the shared cache.

Speech models are not bundled in the ZIP. PrivateType downloads the one you choose directly from NVIDIA on Hugging Face and verifies its pinned size and SHA-256 hash before use.

## Requirements

- 64-bit Windows 10 or Windows 11
- A modern x64 CPU and at least 4 GB RAM; 8 GB or more is recommended
- About 2 GB free disk space for the portable app, model, and working room; add 0.7 GB to keep both models
- [Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable for Visual Studio 2015–2022 (x64)](https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe)

## Privacy

Speech recognition runs locally. PrivateType has no account, cloud-recognition fallback, telemetry, or retained audio. Recent dictations stay in memory only and can be turned off in Settings. Review diagnostic reports before sharing them because application diagnostics can still contain information about your computer environment.
